poster_title: Evaluating LLM Agent Personality and Response Appropriateness
authors: Eswari Jayakumar, Debasmita Mukherjee, Niladri Sekhar Dash
paper_info: Faculty of Computer Science, University of New Brunswick, 2023

panels.headline: LLM-based agents require human-like behavior for better user interactions
content: LLM-based agents are used in various interactive applications.
Personality traits can humanize agents and improve user interactions.
Current evaluation methods are limited and often use fixed psychometric tests.

panels.headline: Evaluating agent responses in real conversational scenarios is challenging
content: Standard psychometric tests do not capture the dynamic nature of conversations.
A flexible question bank is required for open-ended questions.
panels.figure_caption: Sample questions from the novel question bank crafted in this work based categorised by complexity and Bloom's taxonomy of levels of learning

panels.headline: Developed and tested two poetry expert agents with distinct personality traits
content: Poetry expert task using 'Dover Beach' by Matthew Arnold.
Agents: Introvert Agent (IA) and Extrovert Agent (EA) using Langchain framework and GPT-4 mini model.
Flexible question bank designed using Bloom's taxonomy for open-ended questions.
Agent responses evaluated using NLP models, Judge LLM, and human linguistic experts.

panels.headline: Agents were trained on 'Dover Beach' and tested with questions of increasing complexity
content: Evaluation focused on consistency and appropriateness of personality traits.

panels.headline: IA and EA showed distinct and consistent personality traits
content: Distinct personality traits in IA and EA responses.
panels.figure_caption: Evaluation Results of Chat with Introvert Agent (IA) and Extrovert Agent (EA): (a) word cloud of Judge LLM reasoning for IA response evaluations, (b) word cloud of Judge LLM reasoning for EA response evaluations, (c) Frequency distribution of Personality assessed in IA and EA responses by Judge LLM

panels.headline: Interdisciplinary approach effectively evaluates agent responses
content: Interdisciplinary approach combining NLP models, Judge LLMs, and human experts.
Flexible question bank design applicable to various learning tasks and conversational scenarios.
Study limited to two specific personality traits (introvert and extrovert).
Approach may need further validation with a larger set of poems and user interactions.
